- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-90+ values), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — delays in adjusting downward.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to overcorrect upward after recent lows, then fail to return to mean.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are more accurate; longer horizons (e.g., 30d) show greater drift and systematic error.
- Avoids recent high values in forecast, especially when true outcome has just rebounded — underestimates recovery.
- Tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating short-term volatility spikes and overestimating calm periods.
